concerns.location: tasks.md:T025, T036 vs spec.md:FR-003, plan.md:Methodological Rigor
concerns.text: FR-003 and Plan (Methodological Rigor) mandate execution across 10 library sizes (10, 20, 30... 100) to support breakpoint estimation. Tasks T025 and T036 only implement execution for 4 sizes [10, 30, 50, 100]. This gap prevents the statistical analysis (FR-005) from having sufficient data points to identify the 'tipping point'.

concerns.location: tasks.md:T033, T045 vs spec.md:FR-005, plan.md:Methodological Rigor
concerns.text: FR-005 explicitly mandates 'Piecewise Linear Regression' as the method to identify the tipping point. Task T045 implements 'Logistic Regression' as the PRIMARY method and Task T033 demotes the mandated PLR to a 'secondary sensitivity analysis'. No task exists to implement PLR as the primary deliverable required by the spec.

FR-004 strictly defines the pruning trigger as 'after every 10 tasks'. Task T028 implements this as a configurable parameter 'N' with a default of 10. This introduces scope creep and risks violating the 'Pruning Intervention Fidelity' (Constitution Principle VII) which requires the intervention to be applied strictly according to the defined frequency.

Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) requires checksums to be recorded in the `artifact_hashes` map of the state file. Task T015 mentions updating the state file but does not explicitly specify updating the `artifact_hashes` nested key, risking a violation of the Single Source of Truth principle if the structure is incorrect.

Task T030 is a unit test for 'Logistic Regression output format'. Since the spec (FR-005) and Plan mandate Piecewise Linear Regression as the primary method, and Logistic Regression is only a secondary/sensitivity check (if at all), this task targets a methodology that contradicts the primary spec requirement, representing potential wasted effort.
